High level: we bill for "input tokens" (everything you send to the model, including system messages and tool call inputs) and "output tokens" (the tokens produced by the model response and by tool outputs returned via the model). Rounding happens at the request boundary (we bill whole tokens), and streaming does not double-bill — you are charged for the final token counts for input and output per request.

Hi Eva — thanks for the signal. Below are canonical rules and three short worked examples you can paste into procurement. Keeping it concise but unambiguous.

Canonical rules (hosted API):
- Input tokens: every token present in the request payload that is consumed by the model at inference time. This includes system messages, all message roles (user/assistant), and any tool-call input you pass into the model.
- Output tokens: tokens emitted by the model as the response. If a tool is invoked via function-calling, the model's emitted function call (name + JSON arguments) counts as output tokens, and any subsequent text produced by the model after the tool return is additional output tokens.
- Tool-return tokens: if a tool returns data that is then included in the conversation as model output (e.g., a tool's text inserted by the model in the next assistant message), those tokens are billed as output tokens. If you POST a large payload to a tool endpoint outside the model (not injected back into the conversation), that traffic is not billed as model output but may be subject to other integration costs.
- Rounding and aggregation: tokens are counted exactly; billing rounds token counts to the nearest whole token per request (i.e., fractional tokens are not possible). We do not round up per chunk or per streaming frame — final request counts determine charges.
- Prompt concatenation: when you send multi-message contexts, we compute tokenization after concatenation (with special role separators). System message tokens are therefore part of the input token total.
- Special BOS/EOS tokens: model-internal BOS/EOS tokens are included in our tokenizer counts and therefore part of the input/output numbers we bill.

Worked example A — simple prompt + streamed output:
- Request: system ("You are a summarizer") ~60 tokens + user prompt ~120 tokens => input tokens = 180.
- Model emits a 300-token summary streamed via SSE. Output tokens = 300.
- Billing: input = 180 tokens, output = 300 tokens. Rounding: both already whole token counts.

Worked example B — function call with tool response inserted by model:
- Request: system 60 + user 90 => input = 150.
- Model emits a function_call token sequence (counts as output) ~8 tokens to invoke get_lab_results(patient_id). The tool executes and returns a JSON blob (650 bytes) that we insert in the next assistant message. When the model includes the tool-return content in the assistant message, that content tokenizes to 120 tokens of assistant output.
- Billing: input = 150, output = 8 (function call metadata) + 120 (assistant message with tool content) = 128 output tokens.

Worked example C — tool returns large data that is not inserted into the conversation:
- Request: system 60 + user 100 => input = 160.
- Model requests a tool with a small function_call payload (6 tokens). The tool returns CSV that we do NOT inject back into the convo (we store it server-side and only reference an ID). Because the model did not emit the tool data into the assistant message, you are charged: input = 160, output = 6 (function call metadata). Tool-return network bandwidth is separate and not billed as model output.

Edge notes:
- If you re-send the same prompt multiple times (retries), each request is billed independently.
- Caching: we provide prefix/KV caching options for high-volume repetitive prompts which can reduce billed input tokens; happy to run a cache-savings projection for your workload.

Attached: redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf (baseline hosted API tiers + commit discounts) and token-examples.csv with the above examples tokenized under our tokenizer.

If any of the examples don't match your implementation, tell us the exact request payload and we will tokenize it and return a CSV with counts.

Hi Eva — quick answers to the procurement bullets plus next steps. Monica and Karthik are on the thread if you want the technical appendix.

1) Baseline hosted on-demand rates (US):
   - Input tokens: $0.0025 per 1,000 tokens
   - Output tokens: $0.0120 per 1,000 tokens
   (Attached ratecard shows tiered volume pricing and the math examples in token-examples.csv.)

2) Rounding rule (explicit):
   - We compute exact token counts using our canonical tokenizer and then round fractional tokenizer results to the nearest whole token. In practice, tokenizers produce integer token counts; the only place rounding ambiguity can arise is during internal model bookkeeping for sub-token operations — we always round to the nearest integer token for billing (i.e., 0.49 -> 0, 0.5 -> 1). This is consistent and deterministic across requests.

3) Commit/discounts and contract language:
   - For a 12-month $120k annual prepay we can offer a custom discount tier (example: 25% off list for the hosted API line items above) and a billing cadence that fits your procurement cycle (annual prepay or monthly charge against committed balance).
   - We can include minimum throughput SLOs and a limited credit policy for SLA misses in an enterprise addendum. Monica will push a sample SOW/contract language that covers commit, overage handling, and data treatment.

Legal paragraph on tool data (short):
   - When a tool's output is inserted into the assistant message by the model, that text is processed by the model and billed as model output tokens; Redwood does not persist tool payloads by default beyond short-term logs required for debugging and audit unless explicitly configured by the customer. If you use Redwood Private or Dedicated, you can opt to keep tool payloads entirely customer-managed (no Redwood persistence). We will provide precise language for your legal team.
